subject: Move-in inventory report – C, 35 Upper St, London, N1 0PN
body:
Dear Mr Smith,

I moved into C, 35 Upper St, London, N1 0PN today. Please find attached my inventory report, which records the condition of the property at move-in, with photos and timestamps for every issue listed below.

I am sending this so there is a clear record that these issues were already present when I moved in, and so that they are not charged to me from my deposit at the end of the tenancy.

Issues noted (all in the kitchen):

Kitchen
- Wall cabinet door bottom trim: wood-effect trim strip is worn, with the finish peeling and scuffed along its length (cosmetic, already present).
- Wall cabinet door bottom trim (corner): worn and chipped finish on the corner of another cabinet door's bottom trim (cosmetic, already present).
- Wall cabinet underside trim / pelmet: a section appears broken or missing, leaving a gap (cosmetic, already present).
- Cable under wall cabinet: loose cable draped along the underside of the wall cabinet trim, not clipped or concealed (repair needed).
- Worktop to wall tile joint by sink: dark gap where sealant is missing or has failed (repair needed).
- Washing machine door seal: black mould or dirt build-up on the rubber door seal (responsibility to be confirmed).
- Washing machine front panel: torn sticker and adhesive residue on the front (cosmetic, already present).

Repairs
Could you please arrange repairs for the loose cable under the wall cabinet and the missing or failed sealant between the worktop and wall tiles by the sink, and let me know the date when this will be done?

Washing machine door seal
Could you please confirm in writing whether the mould or dirt on the washing machine door seal is something you will deal with, or whether you consider it my responsibility under the tenancy agreement?

For reference:
- Repairs (electrical wiring; sinks and their pipes and drains), and questions about responsibility that depend on the tenancy agreement: GOV.UK – Private renting: repairs, https://www.gov.uk/private-renting/repairs
- Existing cosmetic wear and deposit deductions: Shelter – Deposit deductions for damage and missing items, https://england.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/tenancy_deposits/what_can_your_landlord_deduct_from_your_deposit/damage_and_missing_items

Please could you confirm receipt of this email and the attached report in writing? I will keep a copy of the report with my deposit protection paperwork.

Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,

Anant Shah
